newsitem.title: MALTA: Malta report recommends ending Libya oil deal.
newsitem.headline: Malta report recommends ending Libya oil deal.

text.p: A report sponsored by the Maltese government on the state-owned energy corporation has recommended that an oil supply agreement with Libya not be renewed.
The consultants also urged the government to consider buying electricity from Sicily instead of further extending Malta's power stations, the report said.
The report, issued on Thursday, said Enemalta Corporation was approaching bankruptcy, having been burdened by extensive capital expenditure and low tariffs for electricity.
The situation was made worse when the government in 1995 introduced a value added tax but decided that the corporation would absorb the tax rather than passing it on to consumers.
The consultants, MSD Consultants Ltd, said electricity tariffs should be reviewed and an agreement with the Libyan National Oil Corporation, which expired last month, should not be renewed.
According to the agreement, Enemalta buys oil from Libya at a favourable rate and it is then refined in Sicily at Enemalta's expense.
Malta pays for the crude in products and services.
The consultants said Enemalta would save money by buying oil on the open market.
